title: Comparing Human and Automatic Recognition of Dutch Dysarthric Continuous Speech: A Case Study
abstract: arXiv:2606.30237v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In our goal to develop personalised dysarthric speech recognition (DSR) models, this study compared the recognition performances of human listeners and those of three state-of-the-art, off-the-shelf ASR systems (Whisper-large-V3, Google Chirp 3, and Omnilingual) on the recognition of Dutch continuous read and spontaneous speech from a single speaker with severe dysarthria. Results showed that both humans listeners and the three off-the-shelf ASR systems exhibit word error rates (WER) exceeding 70% on average, indicating that DSR is highly challenging for both humans and ASR systems. Fine-tuning on the dysarthric speech significantly reduced WER. Although overall WERs are still quite high (>23%), the personalised DSR models outperformed the human listeners, and performance is getting closer to being useful for supporting day-to-day communication of dysarthric speakers. translated_title: 荷兰语构音障碍连续语音的人类识别与自动识别比较：一项案例研究
translated_abstract: 为了开发个性化的构音障碍语音识别（DSR）模型，本研究比较了人类听者与三个最先进的现成ASR系统在识别一位重度构音障碍说话者的荷兰语连续朗读和自发语音方面的表现。结果表明，人类听者和三个现成ASR系统的平均词错误率（WER）均超过70%，说明构音障碍语音识别对人类和ASR系统而言都极具挑战性。在构音障碍语音上进行微调显著降低了WER。尽管整体WER仍然相当高（>23%），但个性化DSR模型的表现已经超越了人类听者，其性能正逐渐接近可用于支持构音障碍说话者日常交流的水平。未来的研究应聚焦于改进自发语音上的个性化DSR模型。
tldr: 本研究通过案例研究发现，重度构音障碍的荷兰语语音识别对人类和现成ASR系统都极为困难（WER超过70%），但经过个性化微调的DSR模型性能超越了人类听者，正接近可用于支持日常交流的水平。
en_tdlr: This case study shows that recognizing severely dysarthric Dutch speech is highly challenging for both human listeners and off-the-shelf ASR systems (WER over 70%), but personalized fine-tuned DSR models outperform human listeners and are approaching practical usefulness for daily communication.
